newsitem.title: USA: Gilead sees early '97 Vistide Europe OK.
newsitem.headline: Gilead sees early '97 Vistide Europe OK.

text.p: Gilead Sciences Inc said on Thursday it expects to gain European marketing approval for its lead drug, Vistide, in early 1997.
"We expect to have Vistide approval (in Europe) early next year," Gilead chief executive John Martin told a biotechnology conference organized by The Carson Group and BioCentury Publications.
Vistide, a drug for treating an infection common to AIDS sufferers that can lead to blindness, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in June.

Last month Gilead signed a marketing pact with Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc for marketing Vistide in all countries outside the United States. Under the deal, when Vistide is approved in Europe, Gilead will get a single milestone payment of $10 million and Pharmacia & Upjohn will buy $40 million of newly issued Gilead preferred stock at a premium. Analysts have said they expect the approval in 1997's first quarter.

Martin said Gilead was also actively seeking a major pharmaceutical company partner to help develop and market influenza drugs on which it is working. He said an announcement of a strategic alliance could come in "the near future."
